findings.desc: The restore receipt omitted server-owned before observation, after-boundary terminal run, and Start Recovery database-clock evidence needed to prove ordering and recompute RPO.
Source continuity was represented only by a caller-authored boolean rather than exact before and after source service, deploy, and binding identities.
A suspended recovery cleanup could not retain the mandatory named owner, finance notification, and deletion deadline within 24 hours.
Post-closure internal proofs omitted deploy or run identity and rotated username binding for exact consumer-set coverage.
Quoted boolean and numeric placeholders could produce stringly typed final receipts without a strict schema validator.
Static label checks did not protect authority fields, negative structural cases, or reject unresolved placeholders in final evidence.
A synthetic 15-line Markdown file with PASS labels but none of the required authority sections or bound evidence values was accepted as final evidence.
Matching before and after source continuity sets were not bound to the exact rotated consumer runtime identities.
Start Recovery database clock was not time-bounded to the operator action and lacked its own observation digest.
A cron or worker post-closure proof could reuse the pre-closure rotation run identity instead of proving a fresh run.
An unresolved failed action could be hidden by an unrelated later successful action in the same gate.
